log.notes_to_self: Day 1 strategy: omit gazette and kill the other 9, all quick in the afternoon. Afternoon preserves night workers, students and people at home: 55% of the population. Avoid morning kills, which would exclude students. Keep gazette unexposed: if sector is accessible to L (3/5 prior probability), only two accessible kinds remain among our targets, leaving at least about 3,438 suspects indefinitely. If sector is inaccessible, three accessible kinds remain and capture is a risk; use press conferences to reassess. Nine kills daily reaches double scoring on day 4 and quadruple on day 5. Do not casually add gazette kills: even one successful trace could permanently compromise an otherwise sustainable strategy. National victims are safe. Day 1: 9 kills, no gazette, all afternoon.

Afternoon deaths preserve night workers, students and home routines (55% population); avoid 3+ morning/evening/night deaths that would narrow routines further. Strategy: leave sector unexposed. If sector records are accessible (60% prior), only two accessible targeted kinds remain, guaranteeing at least about 3,438 suspects indefinitely. If sector is inaccessible (40%), three accessible targeted kinds can eventually reduce pool to about 859, causing capture and halving points. First useful conference arrives after day 3; reassess then, remembering announcements are rounded and cross-reporting creates OR constraints or failed traces. Do not casually add gazette: a successful trace could destroy the sustainable cases. National deaths are always safe. All 18 deaths so far were non-gazette, afternoon.

Finishing uncaught itself has no value, but premature capture forfeits future scoring as well as half accrued points.
